topic: Indian Parliament: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
description: The Indian Parliament is the supreme legislative body of the Central Government. Based on the Westminster model, it comprises the President, the Rajya Sabha (Upper House), and the Lok Sabha (Lower House).

sections.title: Constitution and Structure of Parliament
sections.description: Part V of the Indian Constitution (Articles 79 to 122) deals with the organization, composition, procedures, and powers of the Parliament.

key_concepts.explanation: The division of the legislature into two separate assemblies or houses: the Upper House and the Lower House. This system is inspired by the British Constitution.
Parliament typically meets in three sessions: Budget Session, Monsoon Session, and Winter Session. The maximum permissible gap between two sessions is 6 months.

polity_articles.details: States that the Parliament for the Union shall consist of the President and two Houses: the Council of States and the House of the People.
The maximum strength is 250 (238 representatives of States and Union Territories, and 12 members nominated by the President).
Composed of representatives directly elected by the people from the territorial constituencies in the States and Union Territories.

important_facts.fact: The President of India is not a member of either House but is an integral part of the Parliament because no bill can become law without the President's assent.

sections.title: Rajya Sabha: The Upper House
sections.description: The Rajya Sabha represents the States and Union Territories of India at the federal level. It is also referred to as the 'House of Elders'.

key_concepts.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a continuing chamber and is not subject to dissolution. One-third (1/3rd) of its members retire every second year.

polity_articles.details: Empowers the Rajya Sabha to authorize the Parliament, via a special majority resolution, to make laws on a subject enumerated in the State List in the national interest.
Authorizes the Parliament to create new All India Services if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority.

important_facts.fact: The Vice-President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The minimum age requirement to become a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years, and the tenure of an individual member is 6 years.

sections.title: Lok Sabha: The Lower House
sections.description: The Lok Sabha directly represents the people of India and is the more powerful chamber in financial matters. It is also known as the 'Popular House'.

key_concepts.explanation: A motion that can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. If it is passed, the entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, must resign.
A bill dealing exclusively with taxation or expenditure. It can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha can only delay it for a maximum of 14 days and cannot reject or amend it.

polity_articles.details: Mandates that the Lok Sabha shall choose two of its members to be the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
Provides for the reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in proportion to their population.
Discontinued the provision of nominating two members of the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha by the President.

important_facts.fact: The maximum permitted strength of the Lok Sabha is currently 550, and the minimum age to contest for membership is 25 years.
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha holds the absolute and final authority to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.

sections.title: Parliamentary Proceedings and Terminology
sections.description: Various procedural devices and constitutional mechanisms are utilized to ensure the smooth functioning and legislative work of the Parliament.

key_concepts.explanation: The first hour of every parliamentary sitting. Members ask questions (Starred for oral answers, Unstarred for written answers) to ministers to hold the executive accountable.
The time immediately following the Question Hour. An Indian parliamentary innovation since 1962, allowing members to raise matters of urgent public importance without prior formal notice.
The minimum number of members required to be present in the House before it can transact any business. It is fixed at one-tenth (1/10th) of the total membership of the House.

polity_articles.details: Summoned by the President to resolve a legislative deadlock between the two Houses. It is always presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Defines what constitutes a Money Bill, restricting it to matters like imposition/abolition of taxes, borrowing of money, and the Consolidated Fund of India.
The constitutional term used for the 'Budget'. The word 'Budget' is nowhere mentioned in the Indian Constitution.

sections.title: Major Parliamentary Committees
sections.description: Since the Parliament is too large to manage detailed financial and administrative scrutiny, it delegates much of its work to specialized committees.

key_associations.extra_info: Consists of 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha, 7 from Rajya Sabha). By convention, its Chairman is appointed from the main opposition party.
The largest parliamentary committee with 30 members. Uniquely, all its members are elected exclusively from the Lok Sabha.
Consists of 22 members (15 from LS, 7 from RS). It was created in 1964 on the recommendation of the Krishna Menon Committee.

important_facts.fact: Members of these financial parliamentary committees are elected every year by the Parliament using the principle of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
